item.title: Israeli Arab Parties Claim Kingmaker Status in Extra-Tight Vote
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu spent much of election day warning his base that Arab citizens were voting in record numbers. He was right.
item.dc:creator: Shira Rubin

item.title: Judge Questions DOJ Bid to Set Aside 20,000 California Ballots
item.description: A US judge in Los Angeles expressed skepticism about a Trump administration attempt to block California from counting 20,000 mail-in ballots from people the federal government claims are likely non-citizens registered to vote in the upcoming midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Erik Larson

item.title: Bolsonaro Arrives in Miami After Fleeing Brazil, O Globo Says
item.description: Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro arrived in Miami on Tuesday after fleeing his country following a defeat in its presidential election, O Globo reported.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Carvalho and Eric Martin

item.title: US to Issue Visas to Flavio Bolsonaro and His Family
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Michael Oren, former Israeli ambassador to the US, says many Israelis are in shock as Gadi Eisenkot's bloc holds a narrow lead over Benjamin Netanyahu's, but cautions that the result could still change as votes are counted. Rep. Greg Landsman (D-OH) says more voters are casting ballots early and that the numbers suggest a strong night for Democrats in Ohio, while cautioning there are still seven days until Election Day. Rep. Darrell Issa (R-CA) says redistricting could backfire in some states by creating more competitive seats that require significant campaign spending. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Xi’s Corruption Purges Upend Hunt for China’s Next Top Leaders
item.description: As hundreds of China’s top politicians gather in Beijing this week, President Xi Jinping is facing a problem of his own making: His sweeping purges are draining the pipeline he needs to staff senior roles next term.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Rep. Issa Says Redistricting Creates More Seats in Play
item.description: Rep. Darrell Issa (R-CA) says redistricting could backfire in some states by creating more competitive seats that require significant campaign spending. Issa says Flavio Bolsonaro's departure from Brazil could help settle questions around the country's transition of power, while cautioning that his presence in the US does not necessarily mean he will be allowed to conduct political activity from here. On Israel, Issa says Netanyahu would likely continue an aggressive approach toward Iran, Gaza and southern Lebanon if he remains prime minister during another election cycle. Issa also says Congress should address the debt ceiling during the lame-duck session and expects lawmakers to pass the defense authorization bill on a broadly bipartisan basis. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Landsman: Ohio Early Vote Looks Strong for Democrats
item.description: Rep. Greg Landsman (D-OH) says more voters are casting ballots early and that the numbers suggest a strong night for Democrats in Ohio, while cautioning there are still seven days until Election Day. Landsman says Amy Acton and Sherrod Brown are benefiting from voter dissatisfaction with the status quo, but says their races remain uncertain. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Oren Says Netanyahu Could Benefit From Another Election
item.description: Michael Oren, former Israeli ambassador to the US, says many Israelis are in shock as Gadi Eisenkot's bloc holds a narrow lead over Benjamin Netanyahu's, but cautions that the result could still change as votes are counted. Oren says that if Eisenkot cannot assemble the 61 seats needed to form a government, Israel could face another election while Netanyahu remains prime minister. He says time is working in Netanyahu's favor. Oren says a new prime minister could get a grace period in Washington, but adds that Israel's core security policies would be unlikely to change substantially. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tech Rally, Fed Decision & Big Tech Earnings Ahead
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Morgan Stanley Private Wealth Management Executive Director Katerina Simonetti, State Street Investment Management Global Head, Gold Strategy Aakash Doshi, City Analyst Ari Rosa, UPS CEO Carol Tomé, Goldman Sachs Asset Management Global Head of Multi-Asset Solutions Alexandra Wilson-Elizondo, Tola Capital Founder & Managing Director Sheila Gulati, Montage International Chairman, CEO & Founder Alan Fuerstman, Former Fed Governor Randy Kroszner, & RBC Capital Markets Head of US Rates Strategy Blake Gwinn. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: Fed Day Preview (Podcast)
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
The Federal Reserve kicked off a two-day meeting Tuesday after raising interest rates after its previous meeting in September. But as Bloomberg News Federal Reserve and Economy Reporter Enda Curran argues, the Fed is facing its most "confusing" economy yet. Consumer spending is strong, but sentiment is weak, and the economy is experiencing conflicting signals, including high bond yields and slow wage growth.
On today's episode:
Enda Curran, Bloomberg News Federal Reserve and Economy Reporter Chris Merrill, CEO at Harrison Street Asset Management Tim Arndt, CFO at Prologis Justina Lee, Bloomberg News Senior Markets Reporter (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Goldman Sachs Co-CIO: Have To Be Careful About Ownership
item.description: Alexandra Wilson-Elizondo, Global Head of Multi-Asset Solutions at Goldman Sachs Asset Management, says the AI trade now spans multiple asset classes, not just equities. She remains optimistic about technology and sees potential value and opportunities after recent volatility, while noting that heavy investment-grade debt issuance needs to be absorbed by markets. She speaks with Scarlet Fu & Kristine Aquino on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Traders Brace for Fed Day
item.description: The Federal Reserve kicked off a two-day meeting Tuesday after raising interest rates after its previous meeting in September. Bloomberg News Federal Reserve and Economy Reporter Enda Curran says the meeting comes amid the "most confusing economy yet." Meanwhile, Israel voters are heading to the polls for the first national election since the October 7th attack. Bloomberg News Israel Bureau Chief Ethan Bronner breaks down what's at stake. Then, CEO at Harrison Street Asset Management Chris Merrill talks impacts of inflation of alternative real estate investing. Plus, Olympic Marathon Champion and longtime Nike Partner Eliud Kipchoge discusses his running 'World Tour' and how he has worked with Nike over decades to evolve racing gear and push the sport forward. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says High Gas Price a ‘Short-Term Pain’ at Texas Rally
item.description: President Donald Trump returned to Texas on Tuesday in a final attempt to boost Senate candidate Ken Paxton, whose close race in a normally reliable conservative-leaning state has Republicans worried about losing control of the chamber.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason

item.title: Israel Election: Exit Polls Show Netanyahu Trailing Eisenkot
item.description: Three exit polls show Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu trailing challenger Gadi Eisenkot. Voters have turned out in record numbers. The race is still too close to call. Bloomberg's Dan Williams has the latest from Jerusalem. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fed Interest Rate Decision Lands Days Before Midterm Elections
item.description: Higher borrowing costs add to the stress many Americans are feeling as they cast ballots.
item.dc:creator: Enda Curran

item.title: Israeli Vote Deadlocked With Netanyahu Level With Opposition
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot are neck and neck in the first election since the 2023 Hamas attacks, setting up a tense period of negotiations over who will form the next government.
item.dc:creator: Shira Rubin, Galit Altstein and Ethan Bronner

item.title: Nuclear Inspectors See No Evidence Iran Fixed Bombed Sites
item.description: The United Nations nuclear watchdog said it hasn’t detected any efforts by Iran to rebuild nuclear facilities damaged in US and Israeli strikes over the past two years, even as Tehran continues to block inspectors’ access to most of its atomic sites.
item.dc:creator: Magdalena Del Valle

item.title: Supreme Court Allows Deportation Deal Decried as Collusion
item.description: The US Supreme Court left in force what opponents call a “collusive” settlement struck by President Donald Trump’s administration and Texas to cut off an avenue for pausing some deportations.
item.dc:creator: Greg Stohr

item.title: US to Take In Bolsonaro After He Loses Election and Flees Brazil
item.description: The Trump administration plans to issue visas to defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, according to a senior State Department official, confirming multiple reports that the senator fled his country following his loss.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Carvalho and Eric Martin

item.title: Johannesburg’s Infrastructure Crisis Puts South Africa’s Investment at Risk
item.description: Power cuts, water shortages and crumbling roads are undermining Johannesburg’s economy and threatening its ability to retain businesses and attract investment. Can South Africa’s City of Gold turn itself around? On this episode of Next Africa, Jennifer Zabasajja examines the financial pressures and political instability behind Johannesburg’s decline, and whether upcoming local elections could help change its course. Business Leadership South Africa CEO Busi Mavuso explains why companies are being forced to work around failing public services. Ninety One founder and CEO Hendrik du Toit discusses the investment needed to rebuild the city, while Eskom CEO Dan Marokane explains how the utility moved from rolling blackouts to excess generating capacity—and why Johannesburg still faces outages. Plus, Bloomberg South Africa Bureau Chief Alex Parker assesses the city’s infrastructure backlog and prospects for recovery. (Source: Bloomberg)
